sections.title: Three variables that determine your computer vision cost
sections.description: Understanding these drivers helps you budget realistically and scope the right project for your needs.

items.title: 1. Training Data — The Largest Hidden Cost
items.description: Training data is consistently the most underestimated cost in CV projects. Labeled data: $0 if provided. Unlabeled images: $5K–$30K for labeling. Image collection: $8K–$40K. Synthetic data for rare defects: $10K–$35K. Most projects need more labeled data than anticipated.
items.label: Data Readiness

items.title: 2. Inference Latency Requirements
items.description: Real-time CV is significantly more expensive than batch. Batch inference: baseline. Near-real-time (1–5s): +$5K–$10K. Real-time (<200ms): +$10K–$25K. High-speed real-time (<50ms): +$20K–$45K for edge optimization.
items.label: Performance

items.title: 3. Hardware & Deployment Environment
items.description: CV deployment hardware adds to total project cost. Cloud GPU inference: $500–$3K/month. On-premise GPU server: $8K–$30K hardware + $3K–$8K deployment. Edge device: $500–$3K/unit + $5K–$15K engineering. Camera hardware: $200–$5K/camera.
items.label: Infrastructure

sections.title: Computer vision models: open source vs. custom foundation models
sections.description: The CV landscape has evolved dramatically with foundation models — and the build-vs-fine-tune decision has significant cost implications.

blocks.heading: Open source pre-trained backbones (YOLOv8, EfficientDet, Detectron2)
paragraphs: These models are pre-trained on large datasets (ImageNet, COCO) and fine-tuned on client-specific data. They're the default approach for most industrial and commercial CV applications because they dramatically reduce the training data required for good performance. Cost: baseline — this is ClickMasters' default approach.

blocks.heading: Vision foundation models (SAM2, DINOv2, CLIP)
paragraphs: Meta's Segment Anything Model 2 (SAM2) and similar foundation models can perform zero-shot or few-shot segmentation on new object classes without full fine-tuning. They're transformative for applications with very limited training data but add inference latency. Cost: +$5,000–$15,000 for integration and optimization.

blocks.heading: Commercial CV APIs (Google Vision API, AWS Rekognition, Azure CV)
paragraphs: Off-the-shelf CV APIs are appropriate for general object recognition, face detection (with compliance considerations), OCR, and content moderation where categories are general enough to be covered by the API's pre-built models. Cost: typically $0.001–$0.01 per image for API calls + $5,000–$15,000 ClickMasters integration cost.

blocks.heading: Custom models from scratch
paragraphs: Building CV models from scratch without pre-trained backbones is rarely necessary today — the only cases where it makes sense are extremely unusual input modalities (satellite hyperspectral imagery, proprietary sensor types) or cases where legal or IP constraints prohibit pre-trained weights from specific datasets.

sections.title: The questions serious buyers ask before committing to computer vision development
sections.description: No vague promises and no hidden discovery call required to understand the fundamentals.

items.objection: What does computer vision development cost?
items.answer: $40,000–$200,000+. Simple object detection in controlled environment: $40,000–$60,000. GMP pharmaceutical quality inspection: $90,000–$130,000. FDA SaMD medical imaging: $130,000–$200,000+.

items.objection: How long does computer vision development take?
items.answer: 10–28 weeks. Simple detection with adequate training data: 10–14 weeks. Medical imaging with FDA regulatory support: 24–28 weeks+.

items.objection: How much training data do I need for a computer vision project?
items.answer: Minimum: 1,000–2,000 labeled images for simple detection of common objects. Typical: 5,000–20,000 for reliable industrial quality inspection. Rare defects or medical findings: 50,000+ total images with deliberate enrichment of rare examples.

items.objection: Can ClickMasters help collect and label training data?
items.answer: Yes — ClickMasters supports training data collection (camera setup, image capture protocols) and labeling (bounding box, polygon segmentation, pixel-level annotation) as part of CV project scoping.

items.objection: What accuracy should I expect from a computer vision system?
items.answer: Controlled industrial inspection: 92–99%+ precision. Variable outdoor environments: 85–93%. Medical imaging (radiologist-level benchmark): 85–95% sensitivity depending on finding type. ClickMasters quotes expected accuracy from similar past projects and validates it against held-out test data.
